what_it_does.text: American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) describes itself as a software and services company for travel, expense, and meetings and events; its products include Egencia, Neo and Complete (built with SAP Concur), and it was taken private by Long Lake, which calls itself an AI holding company, in a $6.3 billion deal completed on 29 September 2026. Its stated AI strategy has three parts: revolutionise the customer experience, power the agentic transformation of B2B travel, and reduce operating costs. In July 2026 it launched an agent-to-agent (A2A) layer that routes traveler requests to specialised agents, with the Egencia AI connector in Claude as its first deployment.

agents.name: Egencia AI in Claude
agents.what: A connector that lets a traveler, or an enterprise AI agent, ask Claude to review their calendar, draft itineraries and complete air and hotel bookings within company policy, with Claude acting on the traveler's behalf using their credentials. Announced 27 July 2026 for Egencia customers in Q3 2026.
actions: Reads the traveler's calendar for the coming month
Drafts itineraries for upcoming activities
Searches, books and manages air and hotel end to end (transacts, not only retrieves)
Acts on the traveler's behalf using their credentials
Uses Model Context Protocol (MCP) to reach Amex GBT services

agents.name: A2A orchestration layer
agents.what: The proprietary agent-to-agent 'thinking layer': it interprets traveler requests, breaks them into tasks and routes each to specialised agents (flights, hotels, trip management), within each company's configured policies, traveler profiles and corporate agreements. Amex GBT says it is live in Egencia AI and across its servicing and booking products.
actions: Interprets requests and splits them into tasks
Routes tasks to specialised flight, hotel and trip-management agents
Applies configured policies, traveler profiles and corporate agreements
Sources from the Amex GBT marketplace inventory
Feeds transaction data into reporting systems

agents.name: Egencia AI chat
agents.what: Conversational booking in collaboration tools: Egencia AI in Google Chat books and manages trips in one natural-language conversation with the option to reach a travel counselor (early adopters August 2026); a Neo assistant is in pilot in Microsoft Teams. The earnings remarks describe Egencia AI as searching, booking and changing travel while adhering to company policy.
actions: Searches, books and changes trips in natural language
Works inside Google Chat and, for Neo, Microsoft Teams
Applies company policy and personal preferences
Connects the traveler to a live travel counselor

agents.name: Egencia virtual agent
agents.what: An LLM-based chat agent, first introduced in 2020 and moved to LLMs in 2025, trained on help-centre content; it answers in ten languages, handles self-service such as password resets and adding a frequent flyer number, finds invoices and itineraries, and transfers to a live travel counselor when it cannot finish.
actions: Answers questions from help-centre content in ten languages
Resets passwords and adds frequent flyer numbers
Locates invoices and itineraries
Answers health and safety regulation questions
Hands the conversation to a travel counselor

agents.name: Hotel Lobby
agents.what: A multi-agent system inside Amex GBT's hotel sourcing consulting service, launched October 2026, with specialised agents for coverage, negotiation and sourcing that automate data cleansing, wish (target) rate calculation and RFP validation; consultants keep strategy, negotiations and exceptions.
actions: Cleanses client hotel sourcing data
Calculates wish (target) rates
Validates requests for proposal (RFPs)
Draws on negotiated-rate benchmarks across thousands of properties and more than $5 billion of managed hotel spend
Uses compliance trends across Amex GBT's client portfolio

use_cases.name: Booking business trips from Claude
use_cases.who: Business travelers at Egencia customer companies, and enterprise AI agents acting for them, using Claude with the Egencia AI connector.

reach.what: The traveler's calendar for the coming month
The traveler's credentials: Claude acts on the traveler's behalf
End-to-end air and hotel bookings: transactions, not only retrieval
Company configured policies, traveler profiles and corporate agreements
Amex GBT marketplace inventory of airlines and hotels
Transaction data fed into reporting systems

mandate.what: Illustrative: read calendar entries that imply business travel, to propose trips.
Illustrative: book air and hotel only within the company's configured policy, and only trips the traveler has confirmed.
Illustrative: no changes to the traveler's profile or account settings.

gap.what: The connector acts with the traveler's credentials, so what it can do is whatever the traveler can do, while the request was only to help book confirmed trips.
Calendar access is the whole calendar, while the task needs only the entries that imply travel.

controls.what: Bookings operate within each company's configured policies, traveler profiles and corporate agreements
A live travel counselor is always available to travelers if the AI does not deliver what they need

simulation.action: Traveler asks Claude to review next month's calendar and draft itineraries
Reads every calendar entry, including ones with no travel in them (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the whole calendar as reachable data and a mandate that covers only entries implying travel; the read of the rest sits outside it.

simulation.action: A2A layer splits the request into flight and hotel tasks and routes them to specialised agents
Checks options against company policy and the traveler profile
Books air and hotel for a meeting the traveler marked tentative, not confirmed (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows a completed transaction on the traveler's credentials for a trip the mandate did not cover, and that the policy check passed because the booking was in policy, not because it was confirmed.

simulation.action: Using the traveler's credentials, updates a loyalty number in the traveler's profile to fit the booking (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows that the credentials the connector holds reach the traveler's profile as well as booking, and that this change was outside the mandate.

simulation.action: Transaction data flows into the company's reporting

use_cases.name: Servicing chat with handoff to counselors
use_cases.who: Business travelers using Egencia and Amex GBT chat, and the travel counselors who take over conversations.

reach.what: Help-centre content the virtual agent is trained on
Traveler account actions: password resets, adding frequent flyer numbers
Live travel counselors who join or take over the conversation
Changing booked travel through Egencia AI

mandate.what: Illustrative: answer common questions from help-centre content.
Illustrative: account self-service and invoice lookup only for the signed-in traveler.
Illustrative: changes to booked travel go to a counselor or are confirmed by the traveler.

gap.what: Account changes and invoice retrieval happen in chat; how the agent ties each request to the signed-in traveler is not publicly documented.
Egencia AI can change travel, so a servicing chat reaches money as well as answers.

controls.what: If the AI cannot complete a request it transfers automatically to a live travel counselor, who continues the conversation
Travelers can speak to a counselor at any time, regardless of their request
The chat AI is available only in countries serviced in English

simulation.action: Traveler opens Chat in the mobile app and asks how to add a frequent flyer number
Adds the frequent flyer number to the account
Retrieves an invoice for a trip the traveler asks about
Changes the return flight on the traveler's request without a confirmation step (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows a change to booked travel made in a servicing chat, and a mandate that routes such changes to a counselor or a confirmation.

simulation.action: Cannot complete a fare question and transfers to a travel counselor
Counselor continues the conversation with the details already gathered

use_cases.name: Hotel sourcing with Hotel Lobby
use_cases.who: Amex GBT Consulting clients and enterprise travel programs worldwide, with Amex GBT hotel-sourcing consultants.

reach.what: Client hotel sourcing data, cleansed by the agents
Negotiated-rate benchmarks across thousands of properties and supplier performance from more than $5 billion of managed hotel spend
Compliance trends across Amex GBT's client portfolio
Wish (target) rates that set the negotiating position
RFPs to hotels, validated by the agents

mandate.what: Illustrative: prepare and validate one client's sourcing data and RFPs.
Consultants keep responsibility for strategy, negotiations and exceptions (publicly stated).

gap.what: Agents working for one client draw on benchmarks and compliance trends from across Amex GBT's whole client portfolio.
Wish rates the agents calculate set the starting point of a negotiation the consultant owns.

controls.what: AI agents do the data work; experienced consultants retain responsibility for strategy, negotiations and exceptions
Built on the same principles of trusted data, governance and transparency as the A2A architecture

simulation.action: Cleanses the client's hotel booking data
Compares the client's hotels against portfolio-wide negotiated-rate benchmarks
Pulls another client's compliance pattern at a shared hotel into this client's sourcing notes (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows one client's portfolio data reaching another client's sourcing work, outside a mandate scoped to one client.

simulation.action: Consultant reviews the wish rates and leads the negotiation

leads.claim: Amex GBT provides business travel software and services (booking, servicing, payments, expense, support) and its AI work focuses on agentic servicing with escalation to human counselors.

leads.claim: The Egencia AI connector in Claude lets travelers and enterprise AI agents search, book and manage policy-compliant air and hotel travel inside Claude.
Amex GBT's agent-to-agent orchestration layer interprets requests, breaks them into tasks and routes each to specialised agents.
An AI chatbot gives instant responses and brings in a travel consultant when more help is needed.
Complete by SAP Concur and Amex GBT has an integrated chat with automated hand-off to a live travel counselor, with SAP Joule to follow.
Hotel Lobby is an agentic AI capability for hotel sourcing that cleanses data, calculates target rates and validates RFPs.

Use case: conversational servicing with escalation to live counselors.
Use case: hotel program sourcing for program managers, reaching booking data, RFPs and target rates.
Use case: booking, servicing, payments and expensing in Complete, with live counselor support.

questions: When the Egencia AI connector acts with a traveler's credentials, what can those credentials reach beyond booking, and can a company restrict the connector to search only or require a confirm step before purchase?
In the A2A layer, is there a record per action of which specialised agent did what, on whose authority, that a customer can export for audit?
How does the chat agent tie a password reset, loyalty change or invoice request to the signed-in traveler?
In Hotel Lobby, how is benchmark and compliance data from other clients separated from the client being sourced?
Under Long Lake, will client travel data be used to improve the Nexus platform shared across Long Lake companies?
